chunks: And with the preceding chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Nadhr, from Ibrahim ibn Abdul Hamid, from Zaid al-Shahham who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, saying:
"Beware of the dominant power of Allah during the night and during the day." So I asked: "And what is the dominant power of Allah?" He said: "His seizing for the sins."

key_terms.أخذه: His seizing / His taking to account

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the dominant power of Allah (satawat)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) warns his companions to beware of Allah’s ‘satatwat’ — His sudden, overwhelming power — which operates ceaselessly, both night and day. When asked to explain, the Imam defines it as Allah’s seizing of people for their sins. This teaching, delivered to Zaid al-Shahham, reflects a core Shia theological principle: that divine punishment is not arbitrary but is a direct consequence of persistent disobedience, and serves as a constant reminder of moral accountability.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 8. And with the preceding chains of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Nadhr, from Ibrahim ibn Abdul Hamid, from Zaid ibn al-Shahham who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, say: "Beware of the dominant power of Allah, during the night and during the day."
I asked: "What is that dominant power?" He said: "When He seizes you for the sins."
